newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hog prices seen steady-up $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hog prices seen steady-up $0.50 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher as frigid temperatures continued to slow marketings in the western Corn Belt, livestock dealers said.

Icy road conditions and blowing snow in southern Minnesota, northwestern Iowa and southeastern South Dakota played havoc with the hog supply as marketings remained slim and producers struggled to perform routine chores.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota Wednesday could range from $55.50 to $56.00. Illinois top hog prices could range $56.00-$56.50.
Indiana and Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range $54.50 to $55.50 amid firm packer demand for hogs before extremely cold weather moves in by the end of the week, the livestock dealers said.
Temperatures in Iowa and southern Minnesota overnight were expected to plunge well below zero degrees Fahrenheit, with wind chills of 35 to 40 below possible, the dealers said.
The weather-reduced marketings was seen in lighter hog slaughter Tuesday, they said. USDA estimated hog slaughter on Tuesday at 338,000 head, compared with 360,000 a week ago and 365,000 a year ago.
